integration_questions: With the array widened to ±0.06 m, does the signal stay graded on s-bend and slalom, or does it saturate at the outer sensors?
Does the 0.02 m pitch with 7 sensors change steering_oscillation or add lag compared with the 5-sensor array at 0.015 m pitch?
Do the outer sensors at ±0.06 m, which sit beyond the 0.10 m wheel track, cause any problem with the weights or the control signal?
Are there any line-loss events at bend entries now that the array covers a wider span?

intent: Widen the sensor array from ±0.03 m to ±0.06 m with 7 sensors at 0.02 m pitch, keeping the forward row at y=0.07 and the drivetrain from iteration 1. The aim is to keep the line visible and the steering signal graded as the robot drifts toward the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the controller can correct on the s-bend and slalom. Expected result: fewer off-track ends on s-bend and slalom, max_error below about 0.05, progress above 0.4 on the s-bend, and no loss of the oval finishes.
learning: Compare against iteration 1. If max_error falls and s-bend progress rises, edge-of-array saturation was the limit, so the next step is to tune the sensor span or size. If max_error stays near 0.06 with no change, the limit is turn authority, so narrow wheel_track toward 0.09 or raise wheel_radius. If steering_oscillation rises sharply, the 7-sensor sum or the lookahead is adding lag, so pull the row back toward y=0.06.
rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 337.6, up from 184.5) shows the narrower track, larger wheels, lighter mass and forward row helped. The oval now finishes 17 of 20 runs, up from 3. The s-bend (progress 0.24) and slalom (progress 0.18) still end off track. Their max_error is about 0.061 and 0.060, right at the off-track limit. The limit is max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4). Even at body_width 0.18 that gives 0.0575, so the effective limit is 0.06 m for any allowed width, and body width cannot buy margin. The failure is therefore lateral drift reaching 0.06 m before the controller recovers. The rms_error of about 0.028 is modest, so the robot is mostly tracking but overshoots on sharp bends. The current array spans only ±0.03 m. When the robot drifts toward 0.04 to 0.06 m, the line falls off the outer sensors, the signal saturates at the array edge, and the controller gets weak correction just when it needs it most. My change is to widen the array to 7 sensors spanning ±0.06 m at 0.02 m pitch, keeping them at y=0.07 for lookahead. Sensor weights are being set by the Integrator. This keeps the line visible and the signal graded out to the 0.06 m limit, so the controller has authority to act before the edge. I keep wheel_track 0.10, wheel_radius 0.035, mass 0.6 and sensor_size 0.012 unchanged, so the effect of the array can be isolated. Expected result: fewer off-track ends on s-bend and slalom, max_error below about 0.05, and progress above 0.4 on the s-bend. Risk: 7 sensors at 0.02 m pitch raise the sum of readings and may add signal lag, which the Integrator should check.
